title: The Imperfect Active
description: The imperfect active indicative, the augment, and the imperfect of εἰμί.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html: The imperfect is the past of continuing action: ἔλυον, I was loosing. It is made on the present stem with an augment in front and the secondary endings. Before a consonant the augment is ἐ- (λύω, ἔλυον); a verb beginning with a vowel lengthens it (ἀκούω, ἤκουον; αἴρω, ἦρον; α becomes η). In a compound verb the augment comes after the preposition (ἀποστέλλω, ἀπέστελλον), and a preposition ending in a vowel usually loses it (ἀπο- + ἐ- = ἀπε-). The accent cannot go back past the augment.

blocks.caption: ἔλυον, I was loosing
rows: The secondary active endings are -ν, -ς, (none), -μεν, -τε, -ν; the first singular and third plural look alike.

blocks.caption: Imperfect of εἰμί
rows: These forms are not enclitic. After οὐκ and some other words the third singular present is ἔστιν (accent on the first syllable): οὐκ ἔστιν, but οὐκ ἐσμέν.

blocks.caption: μέν … δέ
blocks.html: μέν … δέ sets two clauses side by side: τότε μὲν … νῦν δὲ …, then … but now …; μέν is often best left untranslated.
